title: Vasquez: images may—and must—be adored only with the exemplar, never alone
source_text: LI. Vasquez vero non tantum existimat imaginem uno eodemque actu cum exemplari adorari posse, sed imagines non nisi cum exemplari adorari posse & debere contendit. Perutilis, inquit, & antiqua Theologorum sententia, quam ego veram existimo, est motum adorationis in imaginem, ita in ejus prototypum & exemplar transire, & utrumque sub eandem venerationem cadere, ut nec sola cogitatione, imago per se sine illo, vel ab eo separata adorari possit: Et postea docet, non solum imaginem cum exemplari eodem motu adorationis posse adorari, verum etiam ipsam per se, nisi exemplar contineat, & cum eo conjungatur, non esse alicujus venerationis, & adorationis capacem, ac proinde non nisi cum exemplari, cum quo integrum proximum terminum adorationis constituit, esse colendam. Disputationis centesimae octavae, jam supra allegatae capite tertio.
pass_a_gloss: But Vasquez not only judges that the image can be adored by one and the same act with the exemplar, but contends that images can and ought to be adored only with the exemplar. A most useful and ancient opinion of the Theologians, he says, which I judge true, is that the motion of adoration into the image so passes into its prototype and exemplar, and both fall under the same veneration, that not even by thought alone can the image per se without it, or separated from it, be adored: And afterwards he teaches that not only can the image be adored with the exemplar by the same motion of adoration, but also that it itself per se, unless it contain the exemplar and be joined with it, is not capable of any veneration and adoration, and accordingly is to be cultivated only with the exemplar, with which it constitutes the integral proximate terminus of adoration. Of disputation one hundred eight, already above alleged, chapter three.
pass_b_english: Vasquez goes further: images can and must be adored only with the exemplar—never alone even in thought.
Apart from the joined exemplar the image is not capable of veneration; together they make the integral proximate terminus.

choices.why: Vasquez's own commendation of the ancient view.
